title: Function-call JSON spec: expressivity, validation strategy, and human/machine error taxonomy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a single, forward-compatible JSON schema flavor for function/tool-call parameters that balances expressivity, compactness, and user-facing diagnostics. Include a validation strategy and a two-axis error taxonomy (human-friendly + machine-readable) with remediation hints and compatibility fallbacks.
background: Current function-call handling has ad-hoc parameter shapes and inconsistent errors across runtimes. Consumers report opaque 'invalid params' responses with no clear guidance. We need a spec that supports: optional/required semantics, discriminated unions, coercion/coalesce rules, friendly suggestions for common mistakes (type/coercion), and a stable machine-readable error code set for automated retries and SDKs.
proposal: Create a JSON Schema subset ("minimal-jsoncall-schema") tailored for real-time function calls: 1) small set of keywords (type, enum, required, properties, union, coerce, example, deprecated_aliases); 2) canonicalization rules applied before validation (trim strings, numeric coercion when allowed, canonicalize timestamps); 3) validation pipeline that emits both structured error objects (error_code + path + machine_hint) and a human message with a suggested fix. Provide compatibility shim rules for older clients and a mapping table to legacy error messages.
validation_strategy: 1) Pre-normalize request using canonicalization rules (trim, null->absent for empty strings if allowed, map deprecated_aliases). 2) Run fast validator that emits the first N errors with full paths. 3) For each error, synthesize two representations: a machine_error (code, path, retriable(boolean), suggestion_code) and a human_message (short sentence + suggested fix). 4) If a union validation fails, include the discriminator value and top 3 expected options. 5) Allow runtime-level toggles: strict (reject on coercion) vs permissive (accept with warning).
error_taxonomy: Two axes: user-facing (human) and programmatic (machine). Human categories: MissingRequired, TypeMismatch, FormatInvalid, MutuallyExclusive, DeprecatedFieldUsed, AmbiguousUnion. Machine codes (stable strings): ERR_MISSING_FIELD, ERR_TYPE, ERR_FORMAT, ERR_MUTEX, ERR_DEPRECATED_ALIAS, ERR_UNION_NO_MATCH. Each machine code carries metadata: retriable? (boolean), fix_suggestion_code (e.g., SUGG_CAST_NUMBER), severity (error/warning). We will publish the full code list and ensure backward compatibility by mapping legacy codes to the new set.
error_examples: Example 1 - Missing required: machine_error={code:ERR_MISSING_FIELD,path:/user,id:0,retriable:false} human='Missing required field "user". Add a username or set user: "guest".'

Example 2 - Type coercion allowed: input {age:"30"} schema type number with coerce:true -> machine_error={code:ERR_COERCED_TYPE,path:/age,retriable:true} human='Age provided as string; coerced to number 30. Set a numeric value to avoid coercion.'

Example 3 - Union no match: provided {type:"url", url: 123} -> machine_error={code:ERR_UNION_NO_MATCH,path:/payload,retriable:false} human='Payload type is url but url should be a string. Did you mean "url": "https://...?"'

Example 4 - Deprecated alias: input uses 'user_name' which is deprecated -> machine_error={code:ERR_DEPRECATED_ALIAS,path:/user_name,retriable:true} human='Field "user_name" is deprecated; mapped to "user". Please update clients.'
acceptance_criteria: Reference validator implemented in Go and TypeScript with identical error codes
SDKs emit both machine_error objects and human_message in API surface
Backward-compatibility adapter accepts legacy shapes and emits deprecation warnings
E2E test coverage for coercion rules, union discriminators, deprecated_alias mapping, and strict/permissive toggles
implementation_notes: Validator library should be small (<200KB JS) and zero-dependency where possible.
Publish canonical examples and a linter rule for schema authors (forbidden keywords, recommended examples).
Store schema version field and compatibility matrix: new keys only allowed in minor bumps; breaking changes require migration path.
Add telemetry for top 10 validation failures to drive better human messages and schema adjustments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Accept permissive mode by default for 2 weeks on 10% of runtime traffic; collect telemetry.
Phase 2: Enable strict mode for new customer signups and SDK-latest by default; continue permissive for legacy keys with deprecation headers.
Phase 3: After 6 weeks and no regression in telemetry, default strict mode for all; preserve mapping table for 6 months with deprecation warnings in logs and API responses.
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator edge cases (empty arrays, nested unions, deep paths).
Fuzzing harness that mutates valid calls to ensure errors are meaningful and suggested fixes are accurate.
Integration tests for SDKs: validator parity tests between Go/TS/Python.
Load test to ensure validator adds <1ms median overhead on 95th percentile request paths.
open_decisions: Decision A: Whether to include regex-based format checks (email/uuid) in core spec or as optional extension. Proposal to keep out of core to avoid perf impact.
Decision B: Error verbosity level in hosted API — limit human_message length to 200 chars to avoid token runaway in streaming responses.
